checkedAlternates.risk: Most desks have drawers, so a desk can read as storage.
checkedAlternates.resolution: A desk is used as a work surface first; the drawers are secondary to what you do at it.

checkedAlternates.risk: A shelf is a surface you put books on, which is close to the "put things on" group.
checkedAlternates.resolution: A bookshelf keeps things; a table holds what you are currently using. This is the weakest boundary in the puzzle and is the first thing to check in blind testing.

checkedAlternates.risk: Sofa beds and napping make the sofa a plausible sleeping item.
checkedAlternates.resolution: The usual use of a sofa is sitting, and the bed is the only item whose single purpose is sleep.

checkedAlternates.risk: Side tables sometimes have a shelf or drawer underneath.
checkedAlternates.resolution: The name and the everyday use are both about the surface.

authorReview.notes: Store versus put-things-on is a real semantic edge. Kept because the four-item row is all tables and the three-item row is all closed or shelved storage, which makes the intended reading visible.

blindPlaytest.notes: If the bookshelf splits testers, replace it with a filing cabinet.
